subject.title: feat(onboarding): unified empty-state with provider icons, websites, and recommended installs

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own and order a fixed catalog recommending nine third-party AI tools, or should empty-state recommendations be derived from detector and provider/plugin-owned metadata?
rationale: This choice establishes long-term product endorsement and update ownership; repository policy favors owner-scoped plugin metadata, while the onboarding benefit itself is strongly aligned with first-run usability.

options.title: Derive Recommendations
options.body: Use detector descriptors and provider/plugin manifest metadata as the canonical source, avoiding a parallel hardcoded catalog.

options.title: Approve Core Catalog
options.body: Keep the fixed catalog as intentional product policy with named ownership, selection criteria, update cadence, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Narrow The Catalog
options.body: Recommend only bundled local-runtime providers and move third-party coding-agent install guidance to documentation.

recommendation.title: Derive Recommendations
recommendation.body: Use detector descriptors and provider/plugin manifest metadata as the canonical source, avoiding a parallel hardcoded catalog.

likelyOwner.reason: The related onboarding proposal and assigned maintainer-context review make this person the strongest available owner for the recommendation-policy choice.
